r.정치 구도: A one-party state with the Communist Party above the state; the party's general secretary is also state president and chairman of the Central Military Commission, holding the party, government and military all at once. There are votes, but the party picks the candidates and there is no opposition, so voting never changes the ruling party. Leaders are chosen inside the party at congresses held every five years and confirmed as state president by the National People's Congress the following March. Real power rests with a handful of members of the Politburo Standing Committee, and the 2018 constitution removed the term limit on the state presidency. So the wording that comes out of party congresses, the annual 'Two Sessions' and Central Committee plenums is read as a signal for economic and foreign policy.

t.why: A permanent member of the UN Security Council and the world's second-largest economy, it makes so many parts and finished goods that it is called the world's factory. Through the Belt and Road Initiative it has lent money for ports and railways across Asia, Africa, Europe and Latin America, widening its influence, and through the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation and BRICS it has gathered voices different from the Western-led order. It handles most of the processing of minerals essential to high-tech industry, such as rare earths, so a single export control can shake global supply chains. Rivalry with the United States over trade, chip technology and Taiwan has deepened, and in the South China Sea it faces off with neighbors over islands and waters. It claims developing-country status yet is the world's largest carbon emitter, making it a key party in climate talks.
t.rel: It borders 14 countries by land, among the most neighbors of any country. It competes with the United States on trade, technology and Taiwan, and disputes territory with Vietnam, the Philippines and others in the South China Sea and with India in the Himalayas.
t.korea: The two established relations in 1992, and China is now Korea's largest trading partner. Korea sells chips and chemical intermediate goods and buys finished products and raw materials. After the THAAD missile defense deployment in 2017, China retaliated economically, blocking Chinese group tours to Korea and Korean entertainment, and balancing economics and security became a central task of Korean diplomacy. When Korea relies heavily on China for one item, as in the urea solution shortage, a single Chinese export control reaches Korean daily life right away. China's role on North Korea, the maritime boundary and illegal fishing in the Yellow Sea, and fine dust are also issues between the two.
t.know: China spans more than 5,000 km from east to west, yet the whole country runs on a single time zone, Beijing time.
etext: It produces about a third of the world's manufacturing output. Parts factories, skilled workers, ports and railways are clustered together, so it can make almost anything quickly and cheaply. It holds more than half the world market for electric vehicles, batteries, solar panels and shipbuilding.

It controls most of the refining and processing of battery and chip materials such as rare earths, graphite, lithium and cobalt. Because it can use export controls as a weapon, other countries are redrawing their supply chains.
State banks and government funds channel money into strategic industries. With advanced chips blocked by US export controls, it is spending heavily to make them at home.

A property slump has shrunk household wealth and local government revenue, and the population has begun to fall. With weak consumption, it pushes surplus output into exports, fueling trade friction with other countries.
